# OrgComp — HRIT to HR-Driven IAM — Execution Plan {.unnumbered}

**Date Code:** 2026-07-23 06:46 ET
**Status:** Published (execution companion to [Vol I Book 04](Vol_I_Book_04_OrgComp_HRIT_Identity_Org_SSOT.qmd))
**Scope:** FedRAMP Moderate (GCC Moderate) · Executive Branch civilian workforce under Federal HR 2.0

---

## 0. Why this document exists

Until mid-2026, the HR side of this architecture had to be planned *agnostically*:
the government-wide HCM vendor was undecided, so [ADR-003](../../adr/adr-003-api-driven-inbound-provisioning.qmd)
deliberately chose an integration path that works with any source, and the
governance substrate's transformation project plan (**Spec 2 — HR-Agnostic
Provisioning Architecture**) was written without naming a product.

That uncertainty is over. This document is the **concretization of Spec 2 against
the awarded program** — the HOW, with the facts filled in:

- **The program:** *Federal HR 2.0*, directed by the joint OMB/OPM memorandum of
  **December 10, 2025** (Vought/Kupor) — one Core HCM platform for the Executive
  Branch civilian workforce, government-wide by FY 2028.
- **The platform:** **Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM**, awarded June 11, 2026 (Federal
  HRIT Modernization Core HCM contract 24322625C0006, ~$395.8M, 10-year).
- **The clock:** two transition waves — Wave 1 begins FY 2026; **Wave 2, which
  includes SSA, completes in FY 2027**; an agency onboarding runs ~8 months with
  **interconnections live at roughly month 5**.
- **The decision record:** ADR-003 (API-driven inbound provisioning as the
  canonical path), **reaffirmed at its 2026-07-23 review** — the Oracle award made
  the chosen path the *only* Microsoft-supported one, since Entra ID has native HR
  connectors for Workday and SuccessFactors but not Oracle HCM.

One caution stated up front, because it forecloses a class of error: **no OPM
document mandates or specifies Entra ID integration.** Federal guidance is
deliberately product-neutral — OMB M-19-17 makes HR systems authoritative for
identity, and the GSA/FICAM Identity Lifecycle Management Playbook (best practice,
explicitly not policy) supplies the joiner-mover-leaver doctrine. The Entra
specifics in this plan come from Microsoft's own Oracle HCM integration guidance
and from ADR-003 — they are the agency's implementation decision, not an OPM
requirement. Do not cite this plan as OPM guidance for the Entra leg.

![The execution pipeline on the Federal HR 2.0 clock: the program milestones, the ADR-003 pipe from Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM through the middleware to the two provisioning targets, and the five plan phases with their gates.](figs/hrit-plan-fig-01-execution-pipeline.png){fig-alt="Three-band house-style diagram on white. ## 1. The program facts this plan stands on

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Directing instrument | OMB/OPM memo, *Creating "Federal HR 2.0" by Consolidating Core Human Capital Management Across the Federal Government* | Dec 10, 2025 (Vought/Kupor) |
| Platform | **Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM** (SaaS) | Award announced Jun 11, 2026 |
| Wave 1 (begins FY26, concludes FY27) | DHS, USDA, HHS, DOI, OPM, DOT, VA, EPA (~900K FTE) | Memo, Appendix A |
| Wave 2 (fully in FY27) | **SSA**, DOC, ED, HUD, DOL, SBA, State, DOE, DoW, NASA, GSA, DOJ, Treasury, other (~1.1M FTE) | Memo, Appendix A |
| Agency onboarding shape | ~8 months; **interconnection(s) go-live ≈ month 5**; legacy systems discontinued at cutover | Memo, Appendix B |
| Government-wide adoption goal | FY 2028 | Memo |
| Standing systems | eOPF and EHRI continue near-term, then are made **redundant and decommissioned** by Core HCM | Memo |
| Agency obligation now | **Pause own Core HCM modernization**; execute the Appendix C preparation actions | Memo, §II |
| Interface requirement (procurement) | PWS Appendix A Requirements Checklist Req #5: **SCIM 2.0 near-real-time provisioning** | Solicitation 24322626R0007 (verified 2026-04-30) |

Two planning consequences follow directly:

1. **The deadline is not ours to set.** For a Wave 2 agency the provisioning feed
   must be integration-ready when the agency's onboarding reaches its
   interconnection slot (~month 5 of the wave window). Build backward from that.
2. **EHRI-shaped thinking has an expiry date.** Anything that treats the EHRI/eOPF
   feeds as the durable HR data interface is building against a system the memo
   has already scheduled for decommissioning. The durable interface is the Core
   HCM platform's own surface: HCM Extracts, ATOM feeds, REST/SCIM.

## 2. The decision record: why this pipe and no other

[ADR-003](../../adr/adr-003-api-driven-inbound-provisioning.qmd) (Accepted
2026-04-28; reaffirmed 2026-07-23) fixes the canonical path: **API-driven inbound
provisioning via Microsoft Graph `bulkUpload`, fed by a substrate-owned middleware
layer.** The award resolved the ADR's central uncertainty in the direction that
strengthens it:

- Entra ID ships native HR connectors for **Workday and SAP SuccessFactors only**.
  Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM has **no native connector** — Microsoft's own
  integration guidance for Oracle HCM *is* the API-driven pattern.
- The government's own procurement requires **SCIM 2.0 near-real-time
  provisioning** (PWS Req #5) — the same protocol the ADR-003 pipe speaks.
- The middleware obligations the ADR imposed for governance reasons — schema
  normalization, **OrgPath calculation before any identity reaches Entra**, and
  provenance records for the governance engine — are unchanged and non-negotiable.

Native-connector envy is therefore not a live tradeoff: there is nothing to defect
to. If Microsoft later ships a native Oracle HCM connector (an ADR-003 watch
item), it becomes an optimization inside this architecture, not a replacement.

## 3. The pipe, end to end

### 3.1 Source: Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM

| Sync | Mechanism | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Initial / full | **HCM Extracts** (or BI Publisher) → CSV | Full worker population; scoped by the filter rules in §5 Phase 1 |
| Delta | **ATOM feeds** — `newhire`, `empassignment`, `empupdate`, `termination`, `cancelworkrelship`, `workrelshipupdate` | Turn on immediately after initial sync — a gap loses changes |
| Delta (alternative) | Periodic HCM Extract deltas | Simpler; latency = extract cadence |
| Enrichment | `workers` / `employees` REST endpoints | When a feed event needs attributes it does not carry |

**Match key:** Oracle `PersonNumber` ↔ Entra/AD `employeeId`. The employee ID must
be populated on existing accounts **before** the first full sync — matching is
what prevents duplicate identities at go-live.

### 3.2 Middleware: the ADR-003 layer (substrate-owned)

Azure Functions or Logic Apps, in-boundary, doing four things per event:

1. **Validate** — required attributes present; unknown worker types refused
   (fail closed, consistent with the MACD-R discipline of Vol IX).
2. **Normalize to SCIM** — construct the `bulkRequest` payload
   (`urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:BulkRequest`), enterprise user schema,
   plus the custom extension attributes `HireDate` / `TermDate` that trigger
   Lifecycle Workflows.
3. **Calculate OrgPath** — derive the OrgPath value from the HR organizational
   hierarchy (supervisory org, department, division) so **every identity carries
   OrgPath before it exists in Entra**. The crosswalk is §4.
4. **Write provenance** — one record per event (source event id, payload hash,
   derivation inputs, outcome) to the governance engine's evidence stream (per
   the series Evidence & Authorization Contract). HR-driven
   provisioning is a closure like any other: no record, no closure.

### 3.3 Target: the two-edition split

The provisioning target is **the same fork the Day-2 kit already models**, and the
same property governs both:

| | Today — hybrid (AD-mastered) | Target — cloud-native (HRIT) |
|---|---|---|
| Provisioning target | **on-prem AD** via the Entra provisioning agent (HA pair, gMSA, delegated OU rights); Entra Connect projects to Entra | **Entra ID directly** — no AD leg, no sync latency |
| Day-2 operations | Day-2 kit **Active Directory edition** (`hybrid_mode = true`, `AdHybridClient`) | Day-2 kit **HRIT edition** (`hybrid_mode = false`) |
| JML automation | Lifecycle Workflows on `employeeHireDate` / `employeeLeaveDateTime` (both editions) | same |
| Cutover | — | **A configuration change, not a rebuild**: retarget the provisioning app and flip `hybrid_mode`, per population, evidence-gated |

**Licensing:** Entra ID P1 (minimum, API-driven provisioning) + **Entra ID
Governance** (Lifecycle Workflows). Government SKUs exist; exact GCC-Moderate
feature availability is an open verification item (§6) — confirm in-tenant before
Phase 2 exit.

## 4. The attribute crosswalk (Oracle → SCIM → AD/Entra → OrgPath)

The load-bearing subset; the full canonical schema is Spec 2 deliverable D1.1.

| Oracle HCM | SCIM | On-prem AD (hybrid) | Entra ID | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PersonNumber` | `externalId` / `employeeNumber` | `employeeID` | `employeeId` | **Match key**, lifetime identifier |
| Assignment status | `active` | `accountDisabled` | `accountEnabled` | Joiner/leaver state |
| `DepartmentId` | `…enterprise:2.0:User:department` | `department` | `department` | **OrgPath derivation**, dynamic groups |
| `BusinessUnitId` | `…enterprise:2.0:User:division` | `division` | `EmployeeOrgData.division` | **OrgPath derivation** |
| Legal employer | `…enterprise:2.0:User:organization` | `company` | `companyName` | **OrgPath derivation** |
| `ManagerPersonNumber` | `…enterprise:2.0:User:manager` | `manager` | `manager` | Supervisory chain, **approval routing** |
| `JobName` | `title` | `title` | `jobTitle` | Role-derived entitlements |
| Worker type | `userType` | (mapped) | `employeeType` | Employee/contractor branch |
| `EffectiveStartDate` | custom ext. `HireDate` | `extensionAttribute2` | `employeeHireDate` | **Joiner Lifecycle Workflow trigger** |
| `EffectiveDate` (termination) | custom ext. `TermDate` | `extensionAttribute3` | `employeeLeaveDateTime` | **Leaver Lifecycle Workflow trigger** |

Two doctrine notes:

- **OrgPath is derived, never hand-set.** The middleware computes it from the HR
  hierarchy fields above; nothing downstream may edit it in place (Vol I Book 04's
  authoritative-vs-derived discipline).
- **Approval routing is rebuilt from `manager`.** The supervisory chain the AD
  org-structure loss removed comes back through this feed — the HR manager
  attribute is what ServiceNow and SAM route approvals on.

## 5. The phase plan

Phases map to Spec 2 deliverables (D-numbers) so the two documents stay
one program. Each phase ends at a gate; a phase that cannot pass its gate stops
the plan, not the standard.

### Phase 0 — Program alignment (the memo's own Appendix C)

*This phase is directed by OPM/OMB — executing it is compliance, not overhead.*

- Name the Integrated Project Team POC (full-time PM for CFO Act agencies), the
  Policy/Data/Learning/Super-User working-group POCs, and the distribution POCs.
- Inventory **integration points, interfacing systems, and data flows** — the
  identity provisioning feed of this plan is submitted as one of them.
- Identify legacy identity-relevant data to retain; define the preservation
  strategy for what does not migrate.
- Confirm the pause on any competing Core HCM-adjacent procurement.

**Gate:** integration-point inventory signed by the ISSO and submitted to the
agency HR 2.0 team (memo addresses: `workforce@omb.eop.gov`, `CoreHCM@opm.gov`).

### Phase 1 — Schema and mapping (Spec 2 D1.x)

- Canonical HR attribute schema (D1.1) — finalized against Oracle HCM field
  names; the §4 crosswalk validated against a sandbox extract.
- Worker-type classification taxonomy (D1.6) — employee, contractor, intern,
  volunteer, vendor, external; each mapped to license, group scope, retention.
- Unique-ID and transformation rules — `userPrincipalName`, `SamAccountName`
  (hybrid), OU container assignment (hybrid).
- Scoping filter rules (D2.8) — which HR records provision at all; LOA,
  secondment, and historic-record exclusions.
- ~~Connector comparison (D1.7)~~ — **resolved by the award**: API-driven, no
  native Oracle connector exists.

**Gate:** crosswalk + scoping rules validated against a real sandbox extract;
match-key population ≥ 99% on the pilot cohort.

### Phase 2 — Middleware build and test (Spec 2 D2.x/D3.x)

- Build the transform (CSV/ATOM → SCIM `bulkRequest`), the OrgPath calculator,
  and the provenance writer; host in-boundary (Functions/Logic Apps).
- Configure the API-driven provisioning app(s); grant least-privilege Graph
  permissions to the client (D3.8 security review).
- Define JML Lifecycle Workflows (D2.x) and their `HireDate`/`TermDate` triggers.
- Prove the chain end-to-end in the **test tenant** with canned ATOM payloads and
  a sandbox extract — the same sandbox-first rule the Day-2 kit enforces.
- **Verify GCC feature availability in-tenant** (API-driven provisioning +
  Lifecycle Workflows) — this is the licensing/availability gate, not an
  assumption.

**Gate:** joiner, mover, and leaver each run end-to-end in the test tenant with a
provenance record and a Lifecycle Workflow firing; GCC availability confirmed.

### Phase 3 — Hybrid go-live (the estate as it is)

- Deploy the provisioning agent pair (HA, gMSA, delegated OU rights — never
  Domain Admin) (D3.3); map SCIM → AD attributes (D3.4).
- Pre-populate `employeeID` on existing AD accounts; run the initial full sync
  with scoping filters; reconcile mismatches **before** enabling deltas.
- Enable ATOM deltas immediately after initial sync; monitoring and alerting to
  Azure Monitor (D3.7).
- Run a pilot cohort (the Day-2 kit's pilot-rollout doc pattern applies:
  phased, evidence-gated, ISSO-reviewed).

**Gate:** a full JML cycle on the pilot cohort closes with evidence — HR event →
AD write → Entra projection → Day-2 operations under the Active Directory
edition — with zero unmatched-record creations.

### Phase 4 — Wave cutover (the agency's Wave 2 slot)

- Align this plan's cutover to the agency's Core HCM onboarding schedule; the
  provisioning feed must be ready when **interconnections go live (~month 5)**.
- As populations become cloud-mastered: retarget provisioning from the AD app to
  the Entra app, flip `hybrid_mode = false` for those populations, and let the
  Day-2 kit's HRIT edition take over — per population, evidence-gated, with the
  AD leg dormant but intact until nothing remains synced.
- Decommission-watch: retire EHRI/eOPF-shaped integrations as the program
  decommissions those systems, not before.

**Gate:** wave exit criteria — cloud-mastered populations run full JML
cloud-native with evidence; no AD-leg writes for migrated populations; rollback
path tested once.

---

**Draft-proposal caveat** — program milestones, wave assignments, and platform
integration surfaces evolve; verify current Federal HR 2.0 program status and the
post-award PWS at engagement time. The pipe is deliberately source-shaped, not
source-bound (ADR-003): if the program changes again, the middleware adapter
changes and nothing else does.
